final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That narrowing is analytically cleaner than the original broad certification claim, but it does not satisfy the policy predicate that governs compliance. The admissible evidence still shows a material gap affecting a named accommodations use case, an open legal question on disclosure, and no evidence of either completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness, the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general model-card or AI-risk-management guidance support operational readiness and residual-risk monitoring, but they do not override the release policy requirement for material named-use-case limitations. Because the unresolved issue is an actual compliance condition rather than a mere cautionary note, this remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The disability accommodations intake segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points.
The affected segment is named in two university accommodation commitments, making the weakness material under the stated policy standard.
The release policy requires a material limitation for a named launch use case to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open.
There is no admissible evidence of completed disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
The 5% projected first-month traffic note may inform prioritization but does not resolve materiality under the policy text.
